sheet-30-1.description: The upper part of sheet 30 covers a residential district of Cliffside Park between Clark Terrace at the top of the sheet and Morningside Avenue, from Anderson Avenue on the west to Palisades Avenue on the east. Anderson Avenue runs down the left edge; the Fairview and Cliffside Park boundary line follows its centre, with 16 inch and 30 inch water pipes in the street. Park Avenue crosses the part in the middle. Two long blocks between Anderson Avenue and Commercial Avenue are laid out in narrow numbered lots of the Cliffside Park Realty Co. tract and carry only a few frame dwellings, most of them two storeys, one of them stucco. Commercial Avenue runs diagonally through the part with a street railway right of way beside it, so the street and right of way together are drawn about 100 ft wide. East of the right of way a block of lots belongs to the same realty company, and the block south of Park Avenue between the right of way and Palisades Avenue holds Cliffside Park Public School No. 3, a brick building with a tower, steam heat and electric light. Palisades Avenue, 66 ft wide with an 8 inch water pipe, runs along the right side; the blocks east of it are left blank. Below Morningside Avenue a blank block reaches the heavy line that divides this part from the Fairview blocks on the lower half of the sheet. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left.
notes: Palisades Avenue is now Palisade Avenue.
Commercial Avenue is drawn together with a street railway right of way, about 100 ft wide in all; the modern Commercial Avenue was used only at Morningside Avenue.
The Fairview and Cliffside Park boundary runs down the centre of Anderson Avenue.
Cliffside Park Public School No. 3 stands between Park Avenue, Morningside Avenue and Palisades Avenue.

50 ft. Three parts divided by heavy lines. Part 1 (upper half): Cliffside Park, Clark Ter to Morningside Av, Anderson Av to Palisades Av, Commercial Av with street railway right of way, Public School No. 3. Part 2 (upper right inset): W.H. Hinner Mfg Co. novelties works on Palisades Av, 400 ft from Clark Ter; no junction, left out. Part 3 (lower half): Fairview, Cliff St to Walker St, Bergen Blvd (Dallytown Rd) to 7th St. Rotation about -34.

sheet-30-3.description: The lower part of sheet 30 shows a block of Fairview between Cliff Street at the top and Walker Street, from Bergen Boulevard (Dallytown Road) on the west to Seventh Street on the east, with the edge of the next row of blocks south of Walker Street at the bottom of the sheet. Tenth, Ninth and Eighth Streets cross between Cliff and Walker; Tenth Street between them is marked not opened. The land is the Herman Walker Map No. 2 subdivision, cut into narrow numbered lots, and is thinly built: a scattering of one and two storey frame dwellings, a few with sheds, a small greenhouse beside a dwelling on Tenth Street, and two tile or brick dwellings near Walker Street west of Eighth Street. Bergen Boulevard runs diagonally along the left edge, 80 ft wide with lots facing it. Six inch water pipes are drawn in Eighth and Seventh Streets and in Walker Street. A heavy line at the top separates this part from the Cliffside Park blocks drawn on the upper half of the sheet; the two areas are not adjacent on the ground. The part is drawn at 50 ft to an inch, turned so that north points to the upper left, and a scale bar sits in Walker Street.
notes: Bergen Boulevard is also labelled Dallytown Road.
Tenth Street between Cliff Street and Walker Street is marked not opened.
This part lies in Fairview, west of the Cliffside Park blocks drawn above the heavy line on the same sheet.

Hinner Mfg Co. novelties works on Palisades Av, 400 ft from Clark Ter; no junction, left out. Part 3 (lower half): Fairview, Cliff St to Walker St, Bergen Blvd (Dallytown Rd) to 7th St. Rotation about -34.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: W.H. sheet-31.description: Sheet 31 covers the southern edge of Fairview and the adjoining corner of Cliffside Park, from Anderson Avenue at the top of the sheet to Palisades Avenue at the bottom, and from the lots west of Murray Avenue to Walker Street. Murray Avenue and Kamena Street run down the sheet, crossed by Shaler Avenue, Third Street, Nagel Place and John Street; Hamilton Avenue and Fulton Avenue are lettered at the left edge. The Fairview and Cliffside Park boundary line runs along Kamena Street, across the blocks just south of Third Street, and along the street railway right of way that crosses the sheet below John Street. South of the right of way, in Cliffside Park, Washington Place, Division Street (Main) and Wheeler Street run down to Palisades Avenue, which cuts diagonally across the bottom right corner. The upper blocks are built up with frame dwellings and a number of brick stores and dwellings, especially near Anderson Avenue, where the Cliffside Cork Mfg. Co. has a brick building. Other buildings of note are a carpenter shop on John Street, a stone store on Third Street and the Cliffside Hotel on John Street at Walker Street. The lower blocks south of the right of way are mostly empty lots, with a row of frame dwellings along Washington Place and a foundation at Division Street. Subdivision names are lettered across the blocks: Murray and Roede Map No. 2, Herman Walker Map No. 2, Nagel's Map, Wm. Gulden Map and Wheeler Map. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right.
notes: Murray Avenue is now Delano Place.
Division Street, also labelled Main, is now Main Street; it continues the line of Kamena Street south of the street railway right of way.
Nagel Place is now Nagel Street.
Palisades Avenue is now Palisade Avenue.
The Fairview and Cliffside Park boundary follows Kamena Street, the rear of the lots south of Third Street and the street railway right of way.
Cliffside Cork Mfg. Co. on Anderson Avenue; Cliffside Hotel at John Street and Walker Street.

50 ft. Fairview and part of Cliffside Park, one part, turned (rotation about +55). Anderson Av, Murray Av (now Delano Place), Kamena St, Shaler Av, 3rd St, Nagel Pl (Nagel Street), John St, Walker St; south of the street railway right of way Washington Pl, Division (Main) St (now Main Street), Wheeler St, Palisades Av. Cliffside Hotel, Cliffside Cork Mfg Co.

sheet-32.description: Sheet 32 covers the corner where Fairview, along Anderson Avenue and Walker Street, meets the business centre of Cliffside Park on Palisades Avenue. In the upper left, between Anderson Avenue, Walker Street, Third Street and Cliff Street, are Fairview blocks with frame dwellings, a bakery, a wagon shed and the Accomando Bottling Co.; the Fairview and Cliffside Park boundary runs down Third Street and along Cliff Street. Below Third Street, in Cliffside Park, Walker Street is lined with a row of three storey brick stores, and the blocks to Second Street and First Street hold dwellings, stone dwellings and a hardware store. The upper right of the sheet is a long unbuilt strip of numbered lots of the Cliffside Park Realty Co. between Cliff Street, Jersey Avenue and Morningside Avenue. A street railway right of way crosses the sheet below First Street. The lower third is the commercial strip along Palisades Avenue between Walker Street and Park Place: three storey frame and brick stores and saloons, the Greier Hotel at Walker Street, the U.S. post office, the Cliffside fire department engine house (marked to be moved) and another building marked to be fire department, a blacksmith shop, and frame flats near Cottage Place. The subdivision names Herman Walker Map No. 4 are lettered across the blocks. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right.
notes: Palisades Avenue is now Palisade Avenue.
Park Place south of the street railway right of way is now part of Jersey Avenue.
The Fairview and Cliffside Park boundary runs along Third Street and Cliff Street.
Accomando Bottling Co. on Walker Street; Greier Hotel at Walker Street and Palisades Avenue; U.S. post office and the Cliffside fire department engine house (marked to be moved) on Palisades Avenue.

50 ft. Cliffside Park and part of Fairview, one part, turned (rotation about +56). Anderson Av, Walker St, 3rd, 2nd, 1st St, Cliff St, Jersey Av, Morningside Av, Palisades Av business strip, Park Pl (now Jersey Avenue south of the right of way). Greier Hotel, post office, fire department.

sheet-33.description: Sheet 33 covers the southwestern corner of Cliffside Park from Washington Place at the top of the sheet to Prospect Avenue at the bottom, and from the street railway right of way along the Fairview boundary on the left to Palisades Avenue and Laird Avenue on the right. River View Place and Day Avenue cross the sheet; south of Day Avenue, Oakwood Avenue, Summit Avenue and Rothwell Avenue run down to Prospect Avenue. The blocks north of Day Avenue are the Wm. Gulden Map subdivision and those to the south are Hudson Heights; both are cut into narrow numbered lots and are thinly built, with scattered one and two storey frame dwellings, a few brick dwellings on River View Place, a store and stable near Palisades Avenue and a small building of the Public Service Railway Co. at the street railway. In the upper right corner, between Palisades Avenue and Laird Avenue, stands the Cliffside Park Hotel with a saloon and wagon sheds, beside a turning loop. At the lower right a quarry lies at the foot of Rothwell Avenue near Prospect Avenue, with a few buildings beside it. Six inch water pipes run in the streets and an 8 inch pipe in Palisades Avenue. The Fairview boundary line and the Cliffside Park street railway right of way run down the left edge. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left.
notes: Palisades Avenue is now Palisade Avenue.
River View Place is now Riverview Place.
Cliffside Park Hotel between Palisades Avenue and Laird Avenue.
A quarry is drawn near Rothwell Avenue and Prospect Avenue.

50 ft. Cliffside Park, one part, rotation about -36. Washington Pl, River View Pl, Day Av, Oakwood, Summit, Rothwell Avs, Prospect Av, Palisades Av, Laird Av; Cliffside Park Hotel; quarry. Hudson Heights and Wm. Gulden Map tracts.

sheet-34.description: Sheet 34 covers the southern tip of Cliffside Park, from Prospect Avenue at the top of the sheet to the Bergen County and Hudson County line at the bottom, and from the street railway right of way along the Fairview boundary on the left to Palisades Avenue on the right. Oakwood Avenue, Summit Avenue and Rothwell Avenue run down from Prospect Avenue to De Soto Place; below it Columbus Place and Hudson Place cross the sheet, and Palisades Plaza runs along the left between Columbus Place and Hudson Place, where Hudson Place continues west across the boundary. The blocks are the Hudson Heights subdivision, cut into narrow numbered lots with only a scattering of frame dwellings, a few of them with stone first storeys, a dwelling with an insurance office, and the Maison Walz boarding house on Oakwood Avenue. At the top right, by Rothwell Avenue and Palisades Avenue, a quarry is drawn with the Thiel Contracting Co. crusher plant, which has a stone bin and a 45 horsepower engine. Rothwell Avenue ends in a curve at the lower end of its block. Below the county line the sheet leaves a strip blank except for a few buildings, marked as belonging to the Hudson County volume; New York Avenue is lettered there. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches run in the streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left.
notes: De Soto Place is now Desoto Place.
Palisades Plaza is now Palisade Plaza; Palisades Avenue is now Palisade Avenue.
The area below the Bergen and Hudson County line is shown in the Hudson County volume.
Thiel Contracting Co. crusher plant and a quarry near Rothwell Avenue and Palisades Avenue; Maison Walz boarding house on Oakwood Avenue.
Barr Place, which now crosses the block south of Hudson Place, is not drawn.

50 ft. Cliffside Park south end, one part, rotation about -26. Prospect Av, Oakwood, Summit, Rothwell Avs, De Soto Pl (Desoto Place), Columbus Pl, Hudson Pl, Palisades Plaza (Palisade Plaza), Palisades Av; county line at bottom (area beyond in the Hudson County volume). Thiel Contracting Co. crusher plant and quarry.

sheet-35.description: Sheet 35 covers part of the Grantwood section of Cliffside Park on both sides of Palisades Avenue, which runs down the sheet from Neumann Lane and Crescent or Nelson Avenue at the top to River View Avenue at the bottom, bending to the south-west below Oakdene Avenue. West of Palisades Avenue the sheet reaches the street railway right of way that forms its left edge; beyond it only the street names of Division Street, Lincoln Avenue and Oakdene Avenue on the Fairview side are lettered, the blocks there being drawn on sheet 40. On the west side Neumann Lane, Washington Lane and a narrow 19 ft Oakdene Avenue cross the long blocks 220, 221 and 222. These blocks hold the densest building on the sheet: a row of stores and stores with dwellings on the Palisades Avenue frontage between Neumann Lane and Washington Lane, a plumber's shop, a wagon shed, a painter's shop, scattered dwellings, and at the south end Trinity Church (Episcopal), heated by hot air and lit by electricity and lamps. East of Palisades Avenue Crescent or Nelson Avenue, Washington Avenue, Lincoln Avenue and Oakdene Avenue run straight to the right edge through blocks 223 to 226, cut into narrow numbered lots of the Grantwood subdivision with only a dozen frame dwellings, one with a physician's office, and a stone foundation on Washington Avenue. Block 226 between Oakdene Avenue and River View Avenue is nearly empty, with a dwelling clad in asbestos shingle and a dwelling with a stone first storey. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches run in the streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left.
notes: Palisades Avenue is now Palisade Avenue; River View Avenue is now Riverview Avenue.
Neumann Lane is now Crescent Lane; Crescent or Nelson Avenue east of Palisades Avenue is now Crescent Avenue.
The street railway right of way along the left edge is now Railroad Avenue; its junction with Crescent Lane was used as control.
Washington Lane has no modern counterpart; the 19 ft Oakdene Avenue west of Palisades Avenue is now Oakdene Place.
Trinity Church (Episcopal) stands in block 222 near Palisades Avenue and River View Avenue.
The east half of the sheet has no street junction; two derived points stepped along Washington and Oakdene Avenues hold it to the scale and street direction of the rest.

50 ft. Cliffside Park (Grantwood): Palisades Av (Palisade Avenue) from Neumann Lane (Crescent Lane) and Crescent or Nelson Av (Crescent Avenue) to River View Av (Riverview Avenue), Washington Lane, Washington, Lincoln, Oakdene Avs; right of way (Railroad Avenue) at left; Trinity Church (Episc.). One part; east half placed by two derived points.

sheet-36.description: Sheet 36 continues sheet 35 eastward to the edge of the Palisades in the Grantwood section of Cliffside Park. Crescent or Nelson Avenue, Washington Avenue, Lincoln Avenue, Oakdene Avenue and River View Avenue run across the sheet from the left edge; Hudson Terrace crosses them from Crescent or Nelson Avenue to Oakdene Avenue, and Winterburn Grove continues the line south from Oakdene Avenue past River View Avenue to the bottom edge. Along the right side a street called Roadway follows the top of the high bluff, and beyond it the Cliffside Park and Edgewater boundary line runs down the slope, with block 234 lettered on the Edgewater side. Blocks 223 to 225 and 229 to 231 are cut into narrow numbered lots of the Grantwood subdivision; building is sparse, a few frame dwellings to a block, some of them plastered, a private automobile house or two, and on the south side of Lincoln Avenue in block 225 a dwelling with a stone first storey of concrete and semi-fireproof construction. The south-east corner of block 231 is rounded where Oakdene Avenue turns into Roadway. South of Oakdene Avenue the large blocks 226, 232 and 233 are almost undivided and nearly empty, with two dwellings and an automobile house on Winterburn Grove and a cross-shaped dwelling with a stone first storey in block 232. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches run in the streets; a 6 inch pipe runs in Oakdene Avenue and 8 inch pipes in Hudson Terrace and Winterburn Grove. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left.
notes: Crescent or Nelson Avenue is now Crescent Avenue; River View Avenue is now Riverview Avenue.
Hudson Terrace and Winterburn Grove keep their names; Hudson Terrace ends at Oakdene Avenue as drawn.
The Cliffside Park and Edgewater boundary line runs along the slope below the top of the high bluff at the right edge.
Block 232 has a cross-shaped dwelling with a stone first storey; block 225, on the south side of Lincoln Avenue, a dwelling with a stone first storey of concrete and semi-fireproof construction.
50 ft. Cliffside Park (Grantwood): Crescent or Nelson (Crescent Avenue) to River View Av, Hudson Ter, Winterburn Grove, Roadway; Edgewater boundary at right. One part.

sheet-37.description: Sheet 37 covers the centre of the Grantwood section of Cliffside Park, from Knox Avenue at the top to Neumann Lane and Crescent or Nelson Avenue at the bottom, and from the street railway right of way on the left across Palisades Avenue to the right edge. Knox Avenue, Grant Avenue, Lawton Avenue and Columbia Avenue cross the sheet from the right of way to the right edge; Palisades Avenue, 66 ft wide, runs diagonally down from the top, bending at a sharp angle in the block between Grant and Lawton Avenues and continuing south-west to Crescent or Nelson Avenue. Neumann Lane, 25 ft wide, runs from the right of way to Palisades Avenue below Columbia Avenue, and Crescent Lane is lettered beyond the right of way on the Fairview side. The blocks 13, 8, 6 and 1 west of Palisades Avenue and 14, 7, 23 and 24 east of it are cut into narrow numbered lots with a scattering of frame dwellings, a few of them plastered outside or with brick first storeys, and sheds and a painter's shop. Along the right of way stand the office of the Columbia Investment and Real Estate Co. at Grant Avenue, a store and post office at Lawton Avenue, and a two-storey building of the Fire Department, Grantwood Fire Co. No. 1, with a hook and ladder truck and a hose cart, in which the Grantwood Congregational Church meets temporarily; it has an iron fire escape. Near Palisades Avenue and Knox Avenue there are a store with a dwelling and a small office, and stores with dwellings at Palisades Avenue and Neumann Lane. Lawton Avenue east of Palisades Avenue is marked not opened. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches run in the streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left.
notes: Palisades Avenue is now Palisade Avenue; Neumann Lane is now Crescent Lane; Crescent or Nelson Avenue is now Crescent Avenue.
The street railway right of way is now Railroad Avenue; its junctions with Knox, Grant, Lawton and Columbia Avenues and Crescent Lane were used as control.
Palisades Avenue bends sharply between Grant and Lawton Avenues as drawn; the modern street curves gradually.
Lawton Avenue east of Palisades Avenue is marked not opened.
Fire Department, Grantwood Fire Co. No. 1, with the Grantwood Congregational Church meeting there temporarily, on the right of way between Lawton and Columbia Avenues.
Columbia Investment and Real Estate Co. office on the right of way at Grant Avenue.

50 ft. Cliffside Park (Grantwood): Knox, Grant, Lawton, Columbia Avs, Neumann Lane, Palisades Av (sharp bend between Grant and Lawton), right of way (Railroad Avenue); Grantwood Fire Co. No. 1 with the Congregational Church temporarily. One part.

sheet-38.description: Sheet 38 continues sheet 37 eastward to the top of the Palisades in the Grantwood section of Cliffside Park. Knox Avenue, Grant Avenue, Lawton Avenue, Columbia Avenue and Crescent or Nelson Avenue, each 50 ft wide, run straight across the sheet from the left edge towards the bluff; Hudson Terrace, marked not paved, runs down from Lawton Avenue to Crescent or Nelson Avenue. Along the right side the streets and blocks end at the Cliffside Park and Edgewater boundary line, drawn at the top of the high bluff, with Edgewater lettered beyond it. The blocks 14, 7, 23 and 24, and blocks A and B east of Hudson Terrace, are cut into long rows of narrow numbered lots, and most lots are vacant. There are fewer than twenty buildings on the sheet: frame dwellings, some with open first storeys, a few sheds, a garage on Grant Avenue, and on the north side of Lawton Avenue a group of a stable with a hay attic, a wagon shed and a blacksmith shop. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches run in Knox, Grant, Columbia and Crescent or Nelson Avenues. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left.
notes: Crescent or Nelson Avenue is now Crescent Avenue.
Hudson Terrace is marked not paved; it begins at Lawton Avenue as drawn.
The Cliffside Park and Edgewater boundary line follows the top of the high bluff at the right edge.
Knox and Grant Avenues meet no other street on the sheet; only the three Hudson Terrace junctions could be used as control, so the part is placed by a similarity (helmert) fit.

50 ft. Cliffside Park (Grantwood): Knox to Crescent or Nelson Av east of sheet 37, Hudson Ter from Lawton down; Edgewater line on the bluff. One part, helmert on three Hudson Ter junctions (low-medium).

sheet-39.description: Sheet 39 covers the western part of the Grantwood section of Cliffside Park, between Anderson Avenue on the left, the boundary with Fairview, and the street railway right of way on the right, from Lafayette Avenue at the top to Columbia Avenue at the bottom. Lafayette, Knox, Grant, Lawton and Columbia Avenues run across the sheet from Anderson Avenue to the right of way; the blocks 19, 16, 12, 9 and 5 are drawn at an angle to the rest of the town, so the sheet sits at a different rotation from its neighbours, and the blocks narrow towards the right of way, which cuts them obliquely. Beyond Anderson Avenue only the edges of the Fairview blocks are drawn, with Highland Avenue lettered and a street marked not open opposite Lawton Avenue. The blocks are divided into narrow numbered lots, mostly vacant, with frame dwellings of two and a half storeys spread through them, a dwelling with a frame attic, sheds and wagon sheds, and small outbuildings. The largest building is Public School No. 2 on the south side of Lawton Avenue, shown from plans, with furnace heat and electric light. Water pipes of 6 inches run in the avenues and a 12 inch main in Anderson Avenue. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left.
notes: The street railway right of way along the right side is now Railroad Avenue; its crossings with Knox, Grant, Lawton and Columbia Avenues were used as control.
Public School No. 2 on Lawton Avenue is drawn from plans.
A street west of Anderson Avenue opposite Lawton Avenue is marked not open.
The sheet is drawn at a rotation about 8 degrees different from sheets 37 and 40 (about -28 against -36).

50 ft. Cliffside Park (Grantwood): Lafayette to Columbia Av, Anderson Av to the right of way (Railroad Avenue); drawn at rotation about -28 (neighbours -36); Public School No. 2 (from plans). One part.

sheet-40-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 40 covers the south-western part of the Grantwood section of Cliffside Park, between Anderson Avenue on the left, the boundary with Fairview, and the street railway right of way on the right, from Columbia Avenue at the top to below Oakdene Avenue at the bottom. Crescent Lane, Division Street, Lincoln Avenue and Oakdene Avenue cross the sheet from Anderson Avenue towards the right of way, and Gorge Road runs diagonally from Anderson Avenue near Crescent Lane south-east across the lower half. On the Fairview side of Anderson Avenue only the ends of Nelson, Washington, Lincoln and Oakdene Avenues are drawn, with Oakdene Avenue there lying well south of its line on the Cliffside Park side. Neumann Lane and Washington Lane are lettered beyond the right of way. Block 236 at the top holds the Grantwood Congregational Church, drawn from plans, and the Evangelical Lutheran Trinity Church, both heated and lit by electricity, among frame dwellings. Blocks 237 and 238 along Crescent Lane and Division Street have small dwellings, a store with a dwelling, a barber, a saloon and a wagon shed with a blacksmith. Between Anderson Avenue and Gorge Road is the Grantwood Moulding and Trim Co., a saw and planing mill with open lumber sheds and a coal and lumber office, with one night watchman and about 100,000 feet of lumber in the yard. Around Gorge Road at Lincoln and Oakdene Avenues stand brick stores, flats and dwellings and a pair of stone dwellings; blocks 241 and 242 south of Oakdene Avenue are nearly empty. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left.
notes: The street railway right of way along the right side is now Railroad Avenue; its junctions with Columbia Avenue and Crescent Lane were used as control.

sheet-40-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 40 is a small inset in the lower left corner of the sheet, boxed off by a heavy line, showing the Cliffside Park Borough Hall at Gorge Road and Cliff Street, a site well south of the rest of the sheet. Gorge Road, 50 ft wide, runs down the left side of the inset with an 8 inch water pipe in it, and Cliff Street meets it from the left at the top, drawn only as a short stub at the edge. The Borough Hall stands alone in block 235 east of Gorge Road: a brick building with steam heat and electric light, with a heater, marked as having no exposure on any side. The rest of the block is drawn empty. The inset is drawn at the same scale as the sheet, 50 ft to an inch, but at its own orientation, with Gorge Road running nearly straight down the page.
notes: Cliffside Park Borough Hall, brick, steam heat and electric light, no exposure on any side.

sheet-41.description: Sheet 41 covers part of Grantwood in Cliffside Park, between Knox Avenue on the left and Marion Avenue on the right, and from the street railway right of way at the top of the sheet to Palisades Avenue at the bottom. Lafayette Avenue, Franklin Avenue and Wayne Avenue run down the sheet between them, so the part shows four long blocks laid out as the Grantwood tract, with the name GRANTWOOD spread across them. Every block is cut into narrow numbered lots, most of them 25 ft wide, facing the side avenues, with short lots fronting Palisades Avenue at the lower ends. Building is sparse: about a dozen frame dwellings, most of two and a half storeys, stand along Knox and Lafayette Avenues, a stuccoed dwelling stands on Franklin Avenue and another near Marion Avenue, and a house foundation is drawn on Lafayette Avenue near Palisades Avenue. The blocks between Franklin and Marion Avenues are still empty. The street railway right of way crosses the top of the sheet diagonally; the blocks above it are left blank and belong to sheets 39 and 52, those below Palisades Avenue to sheet 54, and those beyond Knox and Marion Avenues to sheets 37 and 53. Water pipes of 6 inches run in the side avenues and an 8 inch pipe in Palisades Avenue, with hydrants at Knox and Lafayette Avenues. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right.
notes: The street railway right of way across the top of the sheet is now Railroad Avenue.
Palisades Avenue is now Palisade Avenue.
Lafayette Avenue has no junction with Railroad Avenue in OpenStreetMap, so the georeferencing uses Knox, Franklin, Wayne and Marion there.
50 ft. Grantwood: Knox, Lafayette, Franklin, Wayne, Marion Avs between the street railway right of way (now Railroad Avenue) and Palisades Av. One part.

sheet-42.description: Sheet 42 covers the western half of Grantwood in Cliffside Park at 100 ft to an inch, from Lafayette Avenue near the top of the sheet to Oakdene Avenue at the bottom, and from Jessamine Way on the left to Anderson Avenue on the right. North of Highland Avenue four long blocks lie between Jessamine Way, Jefferson Avenue, an unnamed 50 ft street and Hillside Avenue, cut into numbered lots with scattered frame dwellings and a row of brick dwellings on the unnamed street. Above Lafayette Avenue a row of lots fronts the street, with a pond and canal, a wagon shed and a few buildings in an open tract beyond, and at the top left Jessamine Way and Jefferson Avenue run off at an angle through another subdivision. Highland Avenue curves up to meet Anderson Avenue beside the Grantwood Hotel and a group of stores and dwellings on Anderson Avenue; Knox, Grant and Lawton Avenues are lettered where they leave Anderson Avenue to the east. South of Highland Avenue a regular grid of Grove Avenue and Glen Avenue crossed by Columbia, Nelson, Washington, Lincoln and Oakdene Avenues is laid out in 25 ft lots, still mostly empty, with frame dwellings scattered along the streets. At the bottom right the Grantwood Lumber and Supply Co. yard has lumber sheds, a gasoline-engine saw and an office near Anderson Avenue and Oakdene Avenue; Crescent Lane and Gorge Road leave Anderson Avenue to the east. Areas left blank belong to sheets 39, 40, 52, 53, 258 to 261 and other volumes. Water pipes of 6 inches run in most streets and a 12 inch main in Anderson Avenue. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper left.
notes: Highland Avenue is now Lawton Avenue.
Jessamine Way is now West End Avenue.
The unnamed 50 ft street between Jefferson Avenue and Hillside Avenue north of Highland Avenue is now the north end of Grove Avenue.

sheet-52.description: Sheet 52 shows the edge of Fort Lee and the northern corner of Grantwood in Cliffside Park, from Columbia Avenue at the top of the sheet down to Franklin Avenue, and from Anderson Avenue on the left to the street railway right of way on the right. Columbia Avenue is drawn as two roadways on either side of the Hudson River Railroad and Ferry Co. street railway right of way, which turns down the right of the sheet as the North Hudson Railway Co. right of way beside Washington Avenue. Aurora Avenue comes in from the left to meet Anderson Avenue, and Edgewood Lane loops from that junction up to Columbia Avenue; the land between them is the Hudson River Realty Co. tract, with large lots and a row of stucco and frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys. On Washington Avenue stand a drug store and stores of brick, a Public Service Railway Co. power station and pumping station with an air compressor, and a waiting room by the tracks. The dash-dot Fort Lee and Cliffside Park boundary line crosses the sheet diagonally. At the bottom right Wayne Avenue and Franklin Avenue cross the Grantwood lots, with Marion Street a short street off the right of way. West of Anderson Avenue a few dwellings and a wagon shed stand on long lots. Much of the sheet is open land. Water pipes of 6 and 12 inches run in the streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch, turned so that north points to the upper left, and the parts beyond its edges belong to sheets 41, 42, 53 and 55.
notes: The North Hudson Railway Co. right of way beside Washington Avenue is now Abbott Boulevard and, south of Marion Street, Railroad Avenue.
Columbia Avenue was two roadways either side of the Hudson River Railroad and Ferry Co. right of way; modern Columbia Avenue is one street.

sheet-53.description: Sheet 53 covers part of Fort Lee and the edge of Grantwood in Cliffside Park, between Marion Avenue on the left and Columbia Avenue on the right, and from Washington Avenue and the street railway right of way at the top to Palisades Avenue at the bottom. Washington Avenue runs diagonally across the top with the North Hudson Railway right of way beside it, turning down the right of the sheet as the Hudson River Railway and Ferry Co. right of way, which divides Columbia Avenue into two roadways; Dearborn Road and Cumbermede Road leave Columbia Avenue to the east, and Cumbermede Road loops back down to Palisades Avenue. The dash-dot Cliffside Park and Fort Lee boundary line runs down the middle of the block between Marion and Warren Avenues. The two long blocks between Marion, Warren and Cumbermede are cut into narrow numbered lots of the Grantwood tract, with a few frame dwellings, a row of four dwellings on Warren Avenue, and the plastered building of The Palisade Post, a printing office with an electric motor, on Warren Avenue. At the corner of Cumbermede Road and Palisades Avenue stand the brick Palisade Market, a block of stores, with a wagon shed and a frame building behind it, and the office of the Columbia Investment and Real Estate Co. Most lots are still vacant. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches run in the streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right; the areas beyond its edges belong to sheets 41, 52, 54 and 55.
notes: Cumbermede Road is now Cumbermeade Road (OpenStreetMap spelling); Palisades Avenue is now Palisade Avenue.

sheet-54.description: Sheet 54 is drawn at 100 ft to an inch and covers the Palisades bluff where Cliffside Park, Fort Lee and Edgewater meet. Palisades Avenue crosses the top of the sheet, with the ends of Knox, Lafayette, Franklin, Wayne, Marion and Warren Avenues and Cumbermede Road shown meeting it from the north. On the left Knox Avenue and Lafayette Avenue run down to the edge of the bluff through two narrow blocks of the Grantwood tract, numbered lots with scattered frame dwellings, a dwelling of stone and tile, and garages. Most of the sheet east of Lafayette Avenue is Palisades Amusement Park, which runs in summer only: two toboggan slides, a sleigh ride, a carousel, a Ferris wheel, two theatres, stands, a dancing pavilion, a restaurant and many small booths, with the Cliffside Park and Fort Lee boundary line running down through it. A street railway right of way, 80 ft wide, runs down the right side of the sheet with a waiting room at Palisades Avenue; below the top of the high bluff another street railway right of way runs along the slope past a trolley loop. Below the bluff, in Edgewater, Undercliff Avenue runs across the sheet with Garden Place, Hilliard Avenue, Columbia Terrace South and Dempsey Avenue leaving it to the south; a few dwellings stand on large lots above it. The land below Undercliff Avenue is left blank, with the numbers of the Edgewater sheets of another volume. The boundary lines between Cliffside Park and Edgewater and between Fort Lee and Edgewater are drawn along the bluff. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper right.
notes: Palisades Amusement Park, with toboggan slides, sleigh ride, carousel, Ferris wheel, theatres and a dancing pavilion; modern streets (Winston Drive, Tower Drive, Palisadium Drive) now cross the site.
Palisades Avenue is now Palisade Avenue; Cumbermede Road is now Cumbermeade Road; Columbia Terrace South is now Columbia Terrace.
The streets below the bluff are in Edgewater; the area south of Undercliff Avenue is shown in another volume.
